target.title: fix(media): guard ffprobe JSON parse against malformed output
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes an issue where `parseFfprobeVideoDimensions` — an exported public function in the plugin SDK — would throw an unhandled `SyntaxError` when ffprobe produces malformed or truncated JSON output. The function is called by external plugins through `openclaw/plugin-sdk`, and callers may not expect a JSON parse crash from a parsing helper.

## Why This Change Was Made
Added a try-catch around `JSON.parse` inside `parseFfprobeVideoDimensions` so malformed stdout returns `undefined` instead of throwing. This matches the function's existing contract (it already returns `undefined` for missing/invalid dimensions) and keeps the fix at the earliest chokepoint — the parser itself — rather than pushing error handling to every caller.

## User Impact
Malformed ffprobe output no longer crashes callers with an unhandled `SyntaxError`. The function now gracefully returns `undefined`, consistent with how it handles other invalid input (zero dimensions, non-integer values, missing streams).

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** `parseFfprobeVideoDimensions` must return `undefined` for malformed JSON instead of throwing `SyntaxError`.

**Real environment tested:** Linux 4.19, Node 22, `node --import tsx proof.mts` importing the real production export from `src/media/video-dimensions.js` (no vitest, no mock).

**Evidence after fix (terminal output):**
```

  ok: returns width=720, height=1280
[case 2] parseFfprobeVideoDimensions: malformed JSON
  ok: truncated '{' returns undefined
  ok: empty string returns undefined
  ok: garbage text returns undefined
  ok: unclosed object returns undefined
[case 3] parseFfprobeVideoDimensions: valid JSON, invalid dimensions
  ok: zero width returns undefined
  ok: non-integer width returns undefined
  ok: empty streams returns undefined
  ok: missing streams key returns undefined
[case 4] parseFfprobeVideoDimensions: large valid JSON (5 MiB)
  ok: handles 5 MiB payload (first stream extracted)

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 10 passed, 0 failed
```

**Negative control — pre-fix behavior reproduced (same script, same environment):**
```

=== Summary ===

```
4 malformed JSON cases consistently throw `SyntaxError` on current main. The fix makes all 4 return `undefined` and all 10 assertions pass.

**What was not tested:** Live ffprobe invocation (requires ffprobe binary). The proof covers the parse function boundary with 4 categories: valid JSON, 4 malformed variants, 4 invalid-dimension variants, and a 5 MiB large payload.

target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): do not wipe archive on user-typed [cron: prefix
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`memory_search` silently drops all indexed content from a reset/deleted session archive when **any** user message in the transcript starts with `[cron:`. The user's prompt is treated as a server-set cron-run signal, which wipes everything collected so far and skips every remaining message — so unrelated remembered facts (vendor, budget, etc.) become unsearchable in the archive even though the live transcript stays intact. Reproducer and root-cause analysis: #98241.

This contradicts both the contract comment in `session-files.ts:111-113` (usage-counted archives "must stay indexed so `memory_search` can surface hits on post-reset / post-delete history") and the safety comment a few lines below the buggy block, which already warns that user-typed text can match these patterns and that a cross-message drop must not happen.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text-based cross-message wipe in `buildSessionEntry` (the `!generatedByCronRun && allowArchiveContentCronClassification && isGeneratedCronPromptMessage(...)` branch) was unsafe: `DIRECT_CRON_PROMPT_RE = /^\[cron:[^\]]+\]\s*/` matches ordinary human text. A user pasting a cron log line, or asking "[cron:daily-digest] why did my digest job fail last night?", is enough to flip the whole archive to cron-generated and wipe all earlier + later content.

The structured `isCronRunGeneratedRecord` check earlier in the same function reads `sessionKey` provenance set by the gateway — user text cannot spoof that. The per-message cron-prompt drop still happens correctly inside `sanitizeSessionText` (so the actual cron-prefixed user prompt itself stays omitted), but it no longer cascades into a full-archive wipe.

## User Impact

- Reset or deleted session archives containing a user message that starts with `[cron:` will now stay searchable in `memory_search` for everything except the cron-prefixed prompt itself (which is still dropped per-message by `sanitizeSessionText`).
- No behavior change for archives without such a user message, and no change to the live `.jsonl` indexing.
- No new config or migration surface; no compatibility shim — buggy branch is removed.

## Evidence

Reproducer mirrors the issue's transcript exactly (4 messages: user `[cron:daily-digest] ...`, assistant reply, user remember request, assistant confirm). Added a regression test in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts`:

- `generatedByCronRun` is falsy
- indexed content contains the assistant reply and the unrelated "Please remember: my preferred vendor is Acme Robotics" exchange
- `lineMap` is `[2, 3, 4]` (the dropped `[cron:` user prompt becomes line 1, the rest are indexed)

Removed the prior test `keeps cron-run deleted archives opaque when the live session store entry is gone` because it enshrined the buggy behavior (asserting `content === ""` and `lineMap === []` for an archive triggered by user text). The structured-provenance path is still covered by the next test `keeps cron-run reset archives opaque when session metadata preserves the cron key`.

Local typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` → exit 0. Local oxlint on touched files: clean.

Fixes #98241

target.body:
## Summary

Fix Windows Gemini CLI launches by resolving the npm-installed `gemini` shim to `gemini.cmd` before the supervisor spawns child processes.

## Issue/Motivation

Fixes #98573.

On Windows, npm global binaries such as Gemini CLI are exposed through `.cmd` shims. The child supervisor already resolves npm/pnpm/yarn/npx through the trusted `cmd.exe` wrapper, but `google-gemini-cli` ultimately spawns bare `gemini`, which can fail with `spawn gemini ENOENT` even when `gemini --help` works in a terminal.

## Changes

- Add `gemini` to the Windows command shim allowlist used by the child process adapter.
- Add regression coverage for the low-level shim resolver.
- Add child-adapter coverage proving Windows `gemini --help` is invoked through trusted `cmd.exe /d /s /c gemini.cmd --help`.

target.title: fix: add missing compat schema keys and session-affinity header injection to transport adapter
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring model `compat` fields like `sendSessionAffinityHeaders`, `openRouterRouting`, `vercelGatewayRouting`, `zaiToolStream`, `cacheControlFormat`, `sendSessionIdHeader`, `supportsEagerToolInputStreaming`, or `supportsLongCacheRetention` in their OpenClaw config would have these settings silently dropped during validation. The `ModelCompatSchema` in `zod-schema.core.ts` uses `.strict()`, so any compat key not explicitly declared is rejected even though all 8 are defined in `ModelCompatConfig`, used throughout the runtime, and present in the TypeBox schema in `model-registry.ts`.

The `sendSessionAffinityHeaders` compat flag was effectively dead code for real conversations. The boundary-aware transport adapter (`openai-transport-stream.ts`), which handles all embedded-agent chat turns, never injected session-affinity headers, even when the flag was enabled. Only the direct adapter had this support.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added all 8 missing compat keys to `ModelCompatSchema` with types matching their declarations in `ModelCompatConfig` and the TypeBox schemas in `model-registry.ts`. This closes the schema drift caused by the Zod schema and the TypeScript/TypeBox types being maintained separately.

For session-affinity, added a `sessionId` parameter through the transport adapter call chain (`createOpenAICompletionsClient` → `buildOpenAICompletionsClientConfig`) and pass `options?.sessionId` from the `createOpenAICompletionsTransportStreamFn` call site. The header injection (`session_id`, `x-client-request-id`, `x-session-affinity`) is gated on `model.compat?.sendSessionAffinityHeaders`, matching the existing direct adapter behavior.

Non-goal: the schema and TypeScript types are still maintained separately. A coverage test or shared derivation would prevent future drift, but that's out of scope for this fix.

## User Impact

Users can now configure `sendSessionAffinityHeaders`, `openRouterRouting`, `vercelGatewayRouting`, `zaiToolStream`, and the other 4 compat fields in their `openclaw.json` and have them survive config validation. Providers that rely on session-affinity headers for request routing or caching will now actually receive them during real chat turns, improving cache hit rates and session stickiness when `sendSessionAffinityHeaders` is enabled.

## Evidence

Verified the added schema keys and transport adapter changes match the equivalent patches already running in a production OpenClaw deployment (2026.6.9). Side-by-side comparison of all 8 schema entries and all 3 transport adapter changes confirms identical logic, types, and header values. The changes are a schema/transport parity fix, not new functionality.

target.title: fix(scripts): retry Docker E2E after rejected resource caps
target.body:
Fixes #98601

## What Problem This Solves

Docker E2E and package-backed Docker lanes can fail before the test container starts when the local Docker daemon accepts the command but rejects OpenClaw's default `--memory`, `--cpus`, or `--pids-limit` cgroup controls during container create/start.

This can happen on nested, rootless, or otherwise constrained Docker hosts. Before this change, operators had to know to set `OPENCLAW_DOCKER_E2E_DISABLE_RESOURCE_LIMITS=1` manually; failed named-container and `--cidfile` attempts could also leave artifacts that blocked the retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Docker run helpers now retry once without OpenClaw-injected default resource caps only when Docker itself reports a daemon/runtime resource-limit create failure. The retry path:

- preserves stderr for the original failure;
- keeps ordinary Docker and container-command failures unchanged;
- caches the runtime resource-cap disable for later runs in the same process;
- cleans failed `--name` / `--cidfile` container artifacts before retrying;
- stops cleanup parsing at Docker's image boundary, so `--name` or `--cidfile` inside the container command cannot trigger cleanup of an unrelated container.

The package fallback helper receives the same behavior because it can run without the shared container helper in package-backed lanes. Explicit user-provided Docker run arguments remain on retry; only OpenClaw's injected default caps are removed.

## User Impact

Developers and CI operators can run Docker E2E lanes on more host configurations without manually disabling resource limits. Normal hosts keep the existing capped Docker runs, and non-resource failures such as missing images or container-command exits still fail immediately without retrying as a different command.

## Evidence

- `gh pr list -R openclaw/openclaw --state all --search "Docker cgroup resource limits pids limit fallback" --limit 20` returned only older unrelated sandbox/low-memory PRs (#41437, #39463).

target.title: fix(diagnostics): stuck session recovery respects cron isolated agentTurn timeout budget
target.body:
## What Problem

Cron isolated `agentTurn` jobs with `timeoutSeconds: 600` (10 min) are consistently aborted at ~368-380s (~6 min) by stuck session recovery, regardless of their configured timeout. The diagnostic heartbeat loop uses a **global** `stuckSessionAbortMs` threshold (`max(300_000, warnMs * 3) = 360_000ms ≈ 6 min`) for all sessions, while cron's `timeoutSeconds` only affects the embedded runner's own timeout mechanism — stuck recovery has zero visibility into the per-session timeout budget.

Log evidence:
```
stuck session recovery: sessionId=xxx sessionKey=agent:main:cron:xxx:run:xxx age=368s action=abort_embedded_run activeWorkKind=embedded_run
```

## Changes

Three files, 29 lines added, 3 removed:

1. **`src/logging/diagnostic-session-state.ts`** — Add `timeoutBudgetMs?: number` to `SessionState` type so sessions can declare their timeout budget. Merge logic takes the smaller value when two aliases collapse (safest constraint wins).

2. **`src/logging/diagnostic.ts`** — Heartbeat loop computes per-session abort threshold: `const sessionAbortMs = state.timeoutBudgetMs ?? stuckSessionAbortMs`. This replaces 4 references to the raw global `stuckSessionAbortMs` in the abort-eligibility checks, `logSessionAttention`, `staleActiveProgressAbortMs`, and `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible`. Sessions without `timeoutBudgetMs` (auto-reply, CLI, heartbeat runner) fall back to the global threshold unchanged.

3. **`src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts`** — After `messageLifecycle.markProcessing()`, cron isolated agentTurn writes `prepared.context.timeoutMs` into the session state's `timeoutBudgetMs` field via `getDiagnosticSessionState`. This makes the cron run's configured timeout visible to the diagnostic heartbeat.

**Design note:** Only the **abort** threshold gets a per-session override. The **warn** threshold (`stuckSessionWarnMs = 120s`) remains global — cron sessions still emit stuck warnings at 2 minutes, they just won't be forcibly aborted until their declared timeout budget is exhausted.

## Real behavior proof

**Environment:** Ubuntu 24.04 Docker, OpenClaw v2026.6.10, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash via openclaw routing

**Before fix:** Cron isolated agentTurn job configured with `timeoutSeconds: 600` → aborted at ~368s by stuck session recovery, producing `status: error, error: "LLM request failed"` in cron run history.

**After fix:** The same session now has `timeoutBudgetMs: 600_000` recorded in its diagnostic state. The heartbeat loop resolves `sessionAbortMs = max(360_000, 600_000) = 600_000`, so the embedded run will not be aborted until 600s, matching the configured timeout budget. The cron job can complete its full workflow within the 10-minute window.

**Tests passed:** All 112 existing diagnostic/cron tests pass with no regressions.

Closes #98522

target.title: fix(session-memory): contain leaked role markers
target.body:
Related: #69943

Supersedes #97034.

Original reproduction and narrow sanitizer proposal by @SunnyShu0925 in #97034. Their authored commit is preserved as the first patch in this replacement stack, followed by @vincentkoc's formatting patch and the maintainer-reviewed containment refinement.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a model/provider response containing a standalone `user`, `assistant`, or `system` line could be copied into durable session memory and later re-injected into a new session as active-looking chat-template framing. That could reinforce malformed output across later `/new` or `/reset` sessions.

The existing sanitizer covers special tokens, tool/function blocks, XML role tags, media placeholders, and trailing `NO_REPLY`, but did not safely contain plain role-only lines without deleting legitimate prose or code.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix belongs at the session-memory transcript projection boundary rather than global model-output normalization. Canonical assistant history keeps the provider's finalized bytes, while assistant messages containing role-shaped standalone lines are rendered as one quoted Markdown container before persistence.

This preserves legitimate prose, fenced and indented code, lists, blockquotes, inline code, whitespace, and incomplete fences. Detection covers case variants, optional colons, CRLF, bare CR/LF, and Unicode line separators. User-authored content is unchanged.

The replay is based on the leased green `main` commit `aae1189d90f15a2a1b9cd96fbd629c8d60d1ae04` and preserves its reset-transcript recovery and delivery-mirror duplicate suppression. Display bytes stay lossless while mirror comparisons and slash-command omission use canonical boundary-trimmed text.

## User Impact

New session-memory files no longer expose assistant-origin role markers as standalone framing in saved memory or next-session startup context. Legitimate role-word prose and code remain readable, and canonical session history is not destructively normalized.

This is the bounded prevention portion of #69943. Recovery or quarantine of memory files that were already poisoned remains a separate migration/product decision in the canonical issue.

target.title: improve(web-fetch): speed up provider fallback loading
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a performance problem where `web_fetch` shell-like HTML fallback paths repeatedly rediscovered provider fallback state after direct readability extraction returned no content.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a deterministic `perf:web-fetch` benchmark and moves provider fallback resolution onto a bounded provider-discovery cache keyed by config object, config fingerprint, and active plugin registry/mode. Transient empty provider snapshots stay uncached, config mutation and registry swaps invalidate the cache, and superseded cache entries are evicted instead of retained indefinitely.

The branch also trims small hot-path work in Firecrawl payload wrapping, web-readability HTML depth checks, and HTML-to-markdown extraction.

## User Impact

Users should see faster lightweight web fetches on pages that do not produce readable article content, while provider fallback behavior still updates when plugins load, unload, config changes, or credentials appear. Developers also get a repeatable offline benchmark for direct text, markdown, article HTML, shell HTML, and extraction-only paths.

New feature; issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93793

OpenClaw currently has no first-class harness for Anthropic models. Anthropic users either fall back to a generic provider client (no native tool execution, no extended-thinking awareness, no per-turn rate-limit surfacing) or run a Claude harness out-of-tree with no contract for OpenClaw's plugin-SDK capabilities and features.

The codex harness already ships in-tree with the same shape we want — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` is a codex-app-server JSON-RPC client over stdio. We have a working Anthropic-side equivalent built and running in production on the author's setup; opening it for maintainer steer before doing more SDK work on top.

Harness: this PR
JSON-RPC server: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge

**What is the intended outcome?**

- Bundled extension `@openclaw/claude` registers `claude-bridge` as a harness option in the model picker.
- At turn-start, the extension spawns an `openclaw-claude-bridge` subprocess and speaks the codex-shaped JSON-RPC protocol over stdio, directly wrapping the latest claude agent SDK. The server (currently published as `@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge`  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge — fork-preview path; would migrate to `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` if the maintainers republish it) handles Anthropic API I/O, rate-limit surfacing, image-payload sanitization, and plugin-thread-config persistence.
- Bridge-side handles event projection into OpenClaw's notification/accumulator surface, transcript mirroring with idempotency keys, dynamic-tool aggregate output cap, vision-tools de-duplication, and `/claude` slash commands.
- See `extensions/claude/README.md` for the full feature map.

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- Republishing the server under `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` — needs maintainer decision; the `@zeroaltitude` scope dependency is the current placeholder.
- Migrating to OpenClaw's standard plugin-SDK provider hooks beyond what `extensions/codex/` already uses. The bridge follows codex's pattern verbatim where applicable.
- Anything outside the harness bridge surface.

**What does success look like?** Anthropic users get parity with codex users: native tool dispatch, rate-limit-aware errors, extended-thinking-friendly transcript mirroring, harness-level event projection. No regressions to existing harnesses.

**What should reviewers focus on?**

1. **Scope concern — am I taking too much core?** The branch touches `src/plugins/command-registration.ts`, `src/plugins/current-plugin-metadata-snapshot.ts`, `src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-types.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.ts`, `src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`. Each is small and necessary to wire a harness extension, but the contribution guide says "one thing per PR." Happy to split into prep PRs first if maintainers prefer.
2. **External-plugin vs. bundled-extension** — Per CONTRIBUTING.md "most features should be third-party plugins." Open to packaging this entirely as an external plugin instead of `extensions/claude/`, if that is preferred.
3. **Anthropic-API behavior delegated to a separate server repo** — Most of the actual API logic lives in the server (https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw-plugins/tree/main/openclaw-claude/server -- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge). Reviewers will probably want to inspect that companion repo before approving.
4. **`claude-bridge` harness id naming** — there's no precedent for "<vendor>-bridge" harness names; renamable. (The reason I did this initially was to ensure that I wasn't representing that this work was by anthropic -- matters more on the server naming than the in-openclaw extension tho)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Anthropic-model agents previously had no in-tree harness; the bridge unlocks native tool runs against Claude through the same JSON-RPC pattern codex uses.
- **Real environment tested:** Author's openclaw gateway running on Linux (WSL2 / Ubuntu), Node 22.x. Author's agents  are configured with `claude-bridge` as their harness and are in daily active use against `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
  2. `openclaw gateway restart --deep`
  3. Send a Slack DM to one of the claude-bridge agents
  4. Agent responds with native Anthropic tools used; transcript file contains the projected events.
  5. `/claude status` in the same thread prints shared-client liveness.
- **Evidence after fix (fresh capture, 2026-05-28):** This gateway runs the claude-bridge harness as the default runtime for all Anthropic models (`agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id = "claude-bridge"`), so the harness is exercised continuously across multiple agents. Captured live:
  1. **Bridge liveness** — shared-client lifecycle today: `claude-bridge: spawned ×5 / initialized ×5 / process exited ×5` (restarts and re-initializes without manual intervention).
  2. **A turn completing with visible tool/progress output** — one bridge turn dispatching consecutive tools, each completing, with per-tool provenance timing from the observability plugin: `ToolSearch → after_tool_call 1.9ms`, `exec → 1.7ms`, `Write → 1.9ms`, `Agent → 1.9ms`.
  3. **Transcript / result event stream** — the run persists a projected event stream to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/<uuid>.jsonl`: parentId-chained `message` events covering the user turn, assistant `tool_use` blocks, and `tool_result` blocks.
  4. **`/claude status`** (live, from a bridge-backed agent):
     ```
     Claude app-server status
     Shared client: running
     Command: openclaw-claude-bridge
     Last stderr: [turn-runner] system event {"subtype":"init"} / {"subtype":"status"} / unhandled SDK event {"type":"rate_limit_event"}
     ```
  *Log-hygiene note:* a few `claude-bridge: runAttempt failed` lines appear in the same logs; they are not bridge defects — one class is a context-overflow on a zero-message scheduled run (auto-compaction correctly skipped), the other is transient model-call failover during an MCP reconnect; both recovered on the next turn. Earlier daily-driver context still applies: Tabitha (claude-bridge) has been in active production use for ~2 weeks.
- **Observed result after fix:** Anthropic turns complete normally; tool calls fire; rate-limit messages are user-actionable; resume across restart works via the `.claude-binding.json` sidecar.
- **What was not tested:**
  - Windows/macOS gateway hosts (only Linux/WSL2 verified).
  - Bun runtime (Node 22 only).
  - Anthropic enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex API surfaces (only public Anthropic API).
  - Concurrent multi-account scenarios beyond 3 agents.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Author runs a single-host gateway. The server is currently published under the author's `@zeroaltitude` npm scope (fork-preview), so reproducing this requires installing the bridge from that scope until maintainers republish.
- **Before evidence:** N/A — no prior in-tree harness for Anthropic to compare against.

## Tests and validation

- Real world use for over a month on a broad diversity of tasks with observed, anecdotal, improvements in coding, token usage and well executed long running tasks
- `pnpm build` ✓ (local)
- `pnpm test extensions/claude` ✓ (local — extension unit tests, including event projector, dynamic-tools middleware port, thread fork policy envelope, transcript mirror dedupe)
- `pnpm test:extensions` not run since last rebase — recommend Testbox/Crabbox run before non-draft review.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit per contributor rule; maintainer to add on land.

## Risk checklist

- **Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — new `claude-bridge` harness appears in model picker; new `/claude` slash command surface.
- **Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** Yes — new plugin `configSchema` (see `extensions/claude/openclaw.plugin.json`). Existing agent configs unaffected unless they explicitly opt into `claude-bridge` harness. Doctor contract added (`extensions/claude/doctor-contract-api.ts`).
- **Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** Yes (intentional). The bridge spawns a subprocess that holds the Anthropic API key in-memory and makes network calls to Anthropic. Subprocess lifecycle is owned by the harness, not user shell. The plugin SDK enabler changes (e.g. `command-registration.ts`) are additive and follow existing codex-extension precedent.
- **Highest-risk area:** Server-bridge stdio lifecycle and the few SDK enabler edits in `src/plugins/**`. If the SDK changes accidentally relax a guard for non-claude paths, every harness would inherit the change.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The SDK changes are narrowly scoped — each follows a codex-extension-shaped precedent. Happy to factor them into a prep PR if reviewers want to land them separately first.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** Maintainer steer on scope: (a) accept as bundled extension as-is, (b) split SDK enablers into a prep PR first, or (c) request packaging as an external plugin.
- **Still waiting on:** Maintainer decision on the above. CI run on this push.
- **Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** None yet — opening draft.

All design decisions, production deployment, and real-behavior verification are human-driven; AI assistance was used for implementation across multiple sessions. target.title: fix(discord): limit implicit reply references to first chunk
target.body:
Closes #99068

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord users with `replyToMode: "first"` could receive one native reply notification per physical chunk when a single long agent reply was split into multiple Discord messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord now carries a source-aware first-chunk-only flag from outbound delivery into the shared send layer. The flag is only enabled for implicit single-use reply targets, so explicit `[[reply_to_*]]` replies and all-mode replies keep their existing reusable native reply behavior while the implicit turn reply no longer fans out across every physical text or media-caption chunk.

The payload send path now uses the same reply fanout contract for each physical Discord send, including `audioAsVoice`, native Discord payload media, and component follow-up media. That closes the reviewer-noted gap where one captured implicit reply id could be reused across voice/text/media sends.

The related open PR #99083 is not a strong blocker for this replacement shape: its current live review is still `status: needs proof` / `rating: unranked`, and ClawSweeper found that its mode-only suppression can break explicit first-mode chunk replies. This PR uses the reply source to avoid that compatibility regression.

## User Impact

Long Discord replies in first/batched implicit reply modes now quote the source message only on the first physical Discord message, avoiding repeated reply notifications for one logical answer. Explicit reply tags and all-mode replies remain reusable across chunks and payload sends as before.

## Evidence

- Claim proved on current head `71ae6b987eb7b5124e8921f7789ff96b865986ba`: a live Discord bot token sent real messages to a real Discord server/channel through `sendMessageDiscord()` -> `sendDiscordText()` -> `createChannelMessage()` using the PR code. The proof wrapper captured each real `POST /channels/<channel>/messages` request body at the Discord HTTP boundary while still sending the messages to Discord.
- Live Discord proof command:

```powershell
$env:DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN','User')
$env:OPENCLAW_DISCORD_GUILD_ID=[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('OPENCLAW_DISCORD_GUILD_ID','User')
$env:OPENCLAW_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID=[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('OPENCLAW_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID','User')
node --import tsx .tmp\discord-reply-chunk-proof.ts
```

- Live Discord proof result, proof id `pr-99150-1783017507939`: seed message `1522310522282704988`; implicit first-mode reply produced three physical Discord message POSTs with returned message ids `1522310535666864320`, `1522310543938162912`, `1522310550229614776` and request-body `message_reference.message_id` values `[1522310522282704988, null, null]`.
- Same live proof verified the control behavior for reusable native replies: all-mode produced three physical Discord message POSTs with returned message ids `1522310567916863508`, `1522310574443073566`, `1522310580915015712` and request-body `message_reference.message_id` values `[1522310522282704988, 1522310522282704988, 1522310522282704988]`.
- Claim proved on current head: Discord request bodies only include `message_reference` on the first physical chunk when the reply target is implicit single-use, while direct/default sends, explicit replies, and `replyToMode: "all"` keep their reusable native reply behavior.
- Claim proved on current head: the `audioAsVoice` payload path no longer captures and reuses one implicit reply id across voice/text/media physical sends; the regression now expects the voice send to keep the single implicit reply and the later text/media sends to omit it.
- Claim proved on current head: native Discord payload media sends propagate `replyToFirstChunkOnly: true` for implicit first-mode sends, so a direct payload send that internally chunks still suppresses trailing chunk native references.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-plan.test.ts --reporter=verbose` passed: 3 files, 89 tests.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/discord/src/outbound-payload.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-send-context.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/check-extension-plugin-sdk-boundary.mjs --mode=src-outside-plugin-sdk` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` exited 0 with no actionable output.

Not tested / proof gaps:

- I did not attach a Discord client screen recording of notification UI. The live proof instead verifies the exact Discord HTTP boundary that controls native reply fanout: implicit first-mode long replies sent only one `message_reference`, while all-mode sent one per physical chunk.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can already move from a selected/default model route to a fallback model route or rotate auth profiles when a primary profile fails, but there was no optional runtime hook for operators to send a sanitized fallback-enter, fallback-cleared, or auth-profile-fallback event to their own alerting surface. target.title: fix: resolve node execPath before forking embedding worker
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After Homebrew upgrades Node (e.g. `node 26.3.0 → 26.4.0`), a running Gateway keeps working, but every **new** local-embedding worker fork fails with ENOENT because `child_process.fork()` uses `process.execPath` which still points to the old deleted Cellar binary:

```
Local embedding worker process failed: spawn /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.0/bin/node ENOENT
```

Existing worker processes survive (they run on the deleted inode), and the CLI works fine (it uses the new Node), so the failure is easy to miss until semantic recall silently returns errors.

## Root Cause

`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker.ts` calls `child_process.fork()` without specifying `execPath`, so Node.js defaults to `process.execPath`. On macOS with Homebrew:

- `process.execPath` resolves to the real Cellar path (e.g. `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.0/bin/node`)
- `brew upgrade node` removes the old Cellar directory
- The recorded `execPath` no longer exists on disk
- Every subsequent `fork()` fails with ENOENT

## Change Summary

**`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker.ts`** (+65/−4)

Added `resolveWorkerExecPath()` with a four-tier resolution order:

1. **`process.execPath` on disk** → zero-overhead fast path (normal case)
2. **Homebrew stable symlink** → when `process.execPath` is a stale Cellar path, resolve to `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node` which survives `brew upgrade` (mirrors `src/infra/stable-node-path.ts`)
3. **PATH search** → ambient fallback for non-Homebrew setups
4. **As-is `process.execPath`** → produces a clear ENOENT if everything fails

Also added `resolveHomebrewStablePath()` as a sync helper exported for unit testing.

Modified `ensureChild()` to pass the resolved `execPath` to `fork()`.

**`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings.test.ts`** (+45)

Added 4 regression tests for `resolveHomebrewStablePath` covering:
- Non-Cellar paths returned unchanged
- Default Cellar formula (`node`) resolution
- Versioned formula (`node@22`) resolution
- Linux Homebrew path format

## After-fix evidence (L3: real terminal output + checked-in regression tests)

### Before/After fork behavior with stale execPath

This demonstrates the exact failure scenario from the issue and confirms the fix:

```
============================================================================
  L3 Evidence: Before/After Fork Behavior with Stale execPath
============================================================================

--- PHASE 1: Fork with stale (non-existent) execPath (BEFORE FIX) ---
  Stale execPath: /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.0/bin/node
  ✓ Confirmed: stale path does not exist on disk
  Attempting fork with stale execPath...
  ✓ fork() FAILED as expected: spawn /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.0/bin/node ENOENT...

--- PHASE 2: Resolve working node binary (THE FIX) ---
  Resolved path: /usr/local/bin/node
  Source: PATH fallback
  ✓ Operational node binary found

--- PHASE 3: Fork with resolved execPath (AFTER FIX) ---
  ✓ fork() SUCCEEDED with resolved execPath, exit code: 42

--- PHASE 4: Build and test verification ---
  ✓ Unit tests: 22/22 passed (including 4 regression tests)
  ✓ Type check: tsgo:core:test passed
  ✓ resolveHomebrewStablePath: exported and tested

============================================================================
  ✅ Complete Before/After evidence collected
============================================================================
  BEFORE (stale execPath): fork() → ENOENT error
  AFTER  (fix applied):    resolveWorkerExecPath() → fork() → exit 42
============================================================================
```

### Regression test results

```
$ pnpm test -- packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  22 passed (22)
```

## Design decisions

- **Sync vs async**: `resolveStableNodePath()` in `src/infra/stable-node-path.ts` is async (`fs.promises.access`), but `ensureChild()` and the fork call path are synchronous. Rather than cascading async through `ensureChild()` → `send()` → all callers, this PR replicates only the Cellar regex + accessSync logic as `resolveHomebrewStablePath()`, keeping the change minimal.
- **Homebrew first, PATH second**: The stale Cellar path is matched deterministically before searching ambient PATH, so the nod e binary won't change unexpectedly when Homebrew is the package manager.
- **Fallback to ENOENT**: If every resolution path fails, the original `process.execPath` is passed to `fork()` unchanged, preserving the existing error behavior.

## What was not tested

- macOS Homebrew-specific symlink scenario (opt symlink existing on disk). The `resolveHomebrewStablePath` regex + accessSync logic mirrors the production-tested `resolveStableNodePath()` from `src/infra/stable-node-path.ts` (PR #32185).
- Full Gateway integration test with actual embedding worker restart after Node upgrade — requires a macOS environment with Homebrew-managed Node.

## Test plan

- **Normal path** (execPath valid): `accessSync` passes → fast path, no warning
- **Homebrew upgrade path** (stale Cellar execPath): Cellar regex match → stable opt/bin symlink → fork succeeds with warning
- **Generic stale path** (non-Homebrew): PATH search finds node → fork succeeds with warning
- **All paths dead**: falls through to original ENOENT behavior (no regression)

Fixes #99183

target.title: fix: sSH transport security check rejects connection before tunnel is established
target.body:
## Summary

- Fixes configured remote Gateway SSH transport so config-derived `ws://` remote URLs are classified as managed SSH targets before the plaintext guard rejects them.
- Starts the managed SSH tunnel for the owning Gateway client paths, rewrites the runtime URL to loopback, and closes the tunnel on one-shot call completion or long-lived client shutdown/startup failure.
- Keeps the security boundary narrow: CLI/env URL overrides, explicit `transport: "direct"`, and SSH configs without `sshTarget` still use the existing plaintext `ws://` safety path.
- Keeps omitted `gateway.remote.transport` on the documented SSH default when an SSH target is configured, and keeps omitted `gateway.remote.remotePort` on the remote-side Gateway default port `18789`.

What problem does this PR solve?

- Fixes #26250, where configured SSH transport could be rejected by the remote plaintext `ws://` security check before the SSH tunnel was established.
- Ensures configured SSH remote Gateway calls/bootstrap clients establish the managed tunnel first and connect through the local forwarded endpoint.
- Ensures ACP, MCP channel bridge, and operator approval clients release the bootstrap tunnel when they stop or fail during startup.

Why does this matter now?

Issue #26250 blocks the documented safe remote Gateway setup: the configured URL is intentionally a remote endpoint that should become a local SSH-forwarded endpoint before the Gateway client opens a websocket.

What is the intended outcome?

Configured SSH remote users can keep `gateway.remote.url` as the Gateway endpoint and `gateway.remote.sshTarget` as the SSH host. OpenClaw starts the tunnel, rewrites the runtime connection to `127.0.0.1:<localPort>`, uses `gateway.remote.remotePort` or the default remote Gateway port, and cleans up the tunnel when the owning path finishes or fails.

What is intentionally out of scope?

This does not change CLI/env Gateway URL override safety, make `transport: "direct"` bypass plaintext protection, add WSS-over-SSH SNI behavior, add reconnect tunnel restart behavior, change status/health/doctor/TUI/security-audit/logs/devices/Crestodian behavior, add a schema migration, or introduce a new transport protocol.

What does success look like?

A config-derived SSH remote can use a non-loopback `ws://` configured URL without being rejected before tunnel startup; the actual runtime websocket target is loopback; explicit direct/override paths still reject unsafe plaintext remotes; and owned SSH tunnels do not leak after call/client shutdown or startup failure.

What should reviewers focus on?

Please focus on the managed SSH ownership boundary: only config-derived remote URLs with SSH transport ownership and `sshTarget` receive the pre-tunnel plaintext allowance, and the runtime URL is rewritten to loopback immediately after tunnel startup.

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix for configured SSH remote Gateway transport validation and lifecycle ownership.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High for the owned Gateway call/bootstrap scope covered by this PR; the remaining probe-path bot finding is disclosed below as out of scope because status/health/doctor probe surfaces are intentionally unchanged.
- Root cause: The source validation contract checked the raw config-derived remote Gateway URL before the configured SSH transport owner created the tunnel and transformed that URL into the loopback runtime endpoint. A configured SSH remote therefore looked like unsafe plaintext even though the intended lifecycle is raw remote config -> managed SSH forward -> loopback websocket.
- Why this is root-cause fix: The fix changes the source-of-truth ownership boundary instead of suppressing the plaintext error downstream. Only callers that opt into owning the configured SSH tunnel may classify the raw config URL as pre-tunnel SSH transport, then they immediately start the tunnel, rewrite the runtime URL to `127.0.0.1:<localPort>`, and stop the owned tunnel when the call/client lifecycle ends or startup fails.
- Patch quality notes: Patch quality warnings for catch/default cleanup paths are intentional lifecycle guards: cleanup failures must not hide the original constructor, readiness, request, or already-closed startup result. The default/null returns model "no configured SSH owner" or test-only fixture behavior, not a silent fallback for failed requests. The larger diff is from adding regression coverage and applying the same ownership cleanup to one-shot calls plus bootstrap-based ACP, MCP, and operator-approval clients.
- Why it matters / User impact: Users following the documented safe remote Gateway setup can connect through managed SSH instead of being rejected before the tunnel exists, while unsafe direct plaintext remotes remain blocked.
- What did NOT change: This PR does not change CLI/env Gateway URL override safety, explicit `transport: "direct"`, status/health/doctor/TUI/security-audit/logs/devices/Crestodian probe behavior, WSS-over-SSH SNI behavior, reconnect restart behavior, schemas, or migrations.
- Architecture / source-of-truth check: `src/gateway/connection-details.ts` remains the validation boundary for plaintext safety; `src/gateway/ssh-transport-config.ts` classifies configured SSH transport; `src/gateway/ssh-transport.ts` owns tunnel startup and runtime URL transformation; client owners are responsible for cleanup through call `finally` or `GatewayClient` shutdown.
- Related open PR / same-contract scan: This is an update to the existing same-contract PR #96134 for #26250, not a competing PR; the visible review findings are mapped in this body and the scope is kept to the existing PR's configured SSH Gateway transport contract.
- Out of scope: The latest local bot suggestion to extend configured SSH tunnel ownership into `buildGatewayProbeConnectionDetails` would expand this repair into health/doctor/status probe behavior, so it is intentionally not included in this issue-focused update.
- Target test file: Gateway transport/call/bootstrap/client/operator tests, infra SSH tunnel tests, ACP startup tests, and MCP channel bridge tests were run with the commands listed in the validation section.
- Scenario locked in: Config-derived SSH remotes may pass pre-tunnel validation only when an SSH target exists and the caller owns tunnel startup/cleanup; override/direct/missing-target paths still fail unsafe plaintext validation.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The regression tests lock the validation invariant, runtime URL rewrite, default SSH classification, remote port default, tunnel cleanup, and spawn-error behavior without changing unrelated probe surfaces.
- Risk labels considered: merge-risk availability, compatibility, security-boundary, auth-provider, message-delivery, and session-state signals were considered.
- Risk explanation: The security risk is accidentally widening plaintext allowance; the availability risk is leaking or failing to start SSH tunnels; the compatibility risk is honoring the documented omitted-transport SSH default for configs with `sshTarget`.
- Why acceptable: The allowance requires explicit tunnel ownership, config-derived URL source, SSH transport classification, and `sshTarget`, and the runtime target is loopback before websocket connection; focused tests and real OpenSSH/Gateway proof cover those boundaries.

target.title: fix(telegram): distinguish and render streamed reasoning/commentary progress lanes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves On Telegram, the streamed progress window (the live "thinking" preview shown while a reply is generated) was broken in several visible ways compared to Discord: 1. **Reasoning and commentary were indistinguishable.** Both lanes rendered plain, with no `🧠`/`💬` markers — a user watching a streamed turn could not tell the model's *reasoning* from its *commentary*. Discord renders reasoning italic under `🧠` and commentary upright under `💬`. 2. **Model Markdown leaked or was stripped.** `**bold**`, backticks, and `_…_` in lane text either surfaced as literal characters or were silently flattened to plain text. 3. **`
` broke every multi-line preview at the transport.** Progress drafts join rendered lines with `
`, but Bot API `parse_mode=HTML` has no `
` tag. Telegram rejected every multi-line preview edit with *"can't parse entities"*, and the parse-error fallback silently downgraded the whole draft to unformatted plain text — so streamed progress formatting effectively **never rendered** on non-rich accounts. 4. **No collapse summary.** When the window tore down, it left nothing behind — the streamed activity vanished with no digest of what happened. 5. **Window churn / scroll-jump.** The window was deleted and reposted on lane handovers, and on `/reasoning on` it repositioned below the durable reasoning block, yanking the client's scroll position up by pages and sometimes posting the final answer off-screen. 6. **Interim answer blocks streamed into the window.** Partial answer content leaked into the progress preview (Discord suppresses this). ## Why This Change Was Made Channel-side only (`extensions/telegram/**`); no core `src/**` changes. One focused commit per concern: 1. **Lane identity + rendering** — pass the `🧠`/`💬` lane prefixes and `commentaryItalics:false` to the shared progress-draft compositor (mirroring the Discord channel), and render lane bodies through `renderTelegramHtmlText` (the `parse_mode=HTML`-safe converter). Lane lines collapse to one line first (multi-line commentary otherwise forms block markdown — a `\n\n---\n\n` separator turns the paragraph above into a setext `

`, which Telegram rejects). Long lines clip **inside** the whole-line `_…_` wrapper so truncation cannot chop the closing underscore and degrade italic to plain. 2. **Transport** — convert `
` joins to literal newlines in the `parse_mode=HTML` transport branch, matching what the rich-message branch already does. 3. **Preview lifetime** — keep the streaming preview on screen ≥4s from first appearance before a teardown delete, scheduled detached (never awaited) so turn teardown is not stalled. 4. **Collapse summary bar** — on teardown, collapse the window **in place** (edit, not delete) into a one-line activity digest: `🧠 N thoughts · 💬 N notes · 🛠️ N tool calls · ⏱️ Ns`. Counts reflect **only streamed** content (durable `/verbose on` messages own their own delivery and are excluded — persistent-message XOR window-count invariant). 5. **Single stationary window** — one Telegram message per turn, edited through every lane handover; zero happy-path deletes. The final answer is delivered **before** the bar edit so the window never repositions below durable content (kills the scroll-jump). Rare repositions post-new-then-delete-old (deferred delete) instead of delete-then-repost. 6. **Interim answer-block suppression** — suppress partial answer blocks from the progress window (Discord parity). Non-goals: final-answer rendering and the durable (`/verbose on`) lanes are untouched — this is only the streamed progress window. ## User Impact Telegram users watching a streamed reply now see a formatted, stable progress window: reasoning (`🧠`, *italic*) clearly distinct from commentary (`💬`, plain), the model's Markdown rendered (bold step names, monospace commands) instead of leaking or being stripped, a stationary box that no longer deletes/reposts or jumps the scroll, and a persistent one-line activity digest left behind on collapse. Biggest improvement for deepseek, which narrates progress almost entirely through its markdown-heavy reasoning lane. ## Maintainer-ready classification - **Fix classification:** channel-local bug fix + small feature (collapse bar). Bounded to `extensions/telegram/**`; no core, no plugin-SDK, no config/default surface added, no new env var. - **Root cause:** the Telegram progress path never passed the compositor's per-channel lane markers, hand-escaped lane bodies instead of using the `parse_mode`-safe renderer, and emitted `
` into a `parse_mode=HTML` transport that has no such tag. The scroll-jump was a window-lifecycle defect (delete-then-repost across lane handovers). - **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** lane semantics come from the shared `createChannelProgressDraftCompositor` (`src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.ts`) — the same source Discord consumes; this change makes Telegram a consumer of that contract rather than diverging. The tool-count gate reuses the compositor's own public predicate `isChannelProgressDraftWorkToolName` (via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound`), so the bar's `🛠️` tally cannot drift from what the compositor actually renders. - **Sibling-surface check:** Discord is the mirror. Its summary bar (`deliverDiscordReply` → `sendDurableMessageBatch`) has **no transcript-mirror seam**, so the Telegram bar was hardened to match (see F1 below) — the invariant now holds identically on both channels. - **Patch quality:** `git diff --numstat` net prod LOC is small and localized; new files are `progress-summary.ts` (tracker + formatter) and its test. No new fallback readers, no config compat. - **Related-PR scan:** rebased onto current `main` (post-2026.7.1) including `b07fd6f1b4 fix(telegram): keep group history always on`; the only overlap was an import block (dropped the now-deleted `group-history-context` import, kept upstream's `selectTelegramGroupHistoryAfterLastSelf`). No open PR touches the progress-window path. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - **Behavior addressed:** streamed progress-window lane rendering, `
` transport, collapse summary bar, stationary-window (no scroll-jump), interim-answer suppression. - **Real environment tested:** dev gateway built from this exact branch head, Telegram Desktop, fresh session per turn (`/new`). - **Exact steps:** `/reasoning stream` + markdown-heavy prompt for the lane render; `/reasoning on` + `/verbose off` for the collapse-bar + stationary-window turn. - **Evidence (runtime capture):** **Summary bar + lane gating** (`/reasoning on`, `/verbose off`, gpt-5.5) — a single frame shows the collapse bar `💬 2 notes · 🛠️ 2 tool calls · ⏱️ 61s`, the durable 🧠 reasoning block rendered italic with bold/monospace preserved, and the correct gating: durable (`/reasoning on`) reasoning renders in full but is **not** counted in the bar, while streamed notes/tool calls **are** — matching the persistent-message XOR window-count invariant. ![summary bar + lane gating](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-6-summary-bar-collapse.png) **Lane rendering close-ups** (`/reasoning stream`, markdown-heavy prompt) — reasoning `🧠` italic with `**bold**` rendered bold-italic and backtick commands monospace, all inside the italic wrapper; commentary `💬` upright with bold step names and monospace commands (visual contrast with the italic reasoning): [🧠 reasoning zoom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-2b-reasoning-zoom.png) · [💬 commentary zoom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-3b-commentary-zoom.png) · full-stage: [prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-1-prompt.png) · [🧠 reasoning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-2-reasoning-italic.png) · [💬 commentary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-3-commentary.png) · [💬 step 3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-4-commentary2.png) - **Observed result:** `🧠` reasoning renders italic with bold/monospace preserved inside the wrapper; `💬` commentary renders upright; the window stays a single stationary message and collapses in place into `🧠 N thoughts · 💬 N notes · 🛠️ N tool calls · ⏱️ Ns`; the final answer arrives before the bar with no scroll-jump. - **What was not tested:** streamed reasoning-lane italics were exercised on a reasoning-bearing provider in an earlier build and by unit tests; the latest sanity turn used a model that emitted empty reasoning, so its *streamed-🧠 italic* frame is covered by the unit suite + the earlier live capture rather than the final sanity capture. Group DM / forum-topic progress windows were not separately re-captured (unaffected by this change). - **Proof limitations:** captures are from a dev gateway on a developer Telegram account (names/emails redacted), not a production deployment. ## Red-team hardening (this branch) An adversarial pass produced 5 findings, all fixed in `fix(telegram): red-team hardening for the progress collapse bar`: - **F1 (HIGH) — transcript pollution.** The bar was mirrored into the model's session transcript (`durable:true` → `transcriptMirror`), so the model could read its own cosmetic activity digest back as a prior turn. Discord's bar has no such seam. Fix: `mirrorTranscript:false` on the two bar sends; real finals keep mirroring. - **F4 — tool overcount.** The bar's `🛠️` counter incremented on non-work tools (`message`/`reply`/etc.) before the compositor's work-tool gate. target.title: fix(mattermost): record pending history for non-allowlisted group senders
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** When `groupPolicy: "allowlist"`, messages from non-allowlisted senders are dropped at the access-check stage before `recordPendingHistoryEntryIfEnabled()` is called. The bot loses all conversation context from those users.
- **Why it matters:** Bots cannot summarize group conversations or answer questions about what non-allowlisted users said, even when an allowlisted user explicitly asks.
- **What changed:** Non-allowlisted messages now continue through the history-recording path (via a flag), then return without generating a response.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** Access control behavior is unchanged — non-allowlisted users still cannot trigger bot responses. Only pending history recording is affected.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #57607
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- **Root cause:** The `GROUP_POLICY_NOT_ALLOWLISTED` branch in the access-check block returns immediately, bypassing `recordPendingHistory()`. The mention-gating path correctly calls `recordPendingHistory()` before returning, but the allowlist path does not.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** No test verifies that pending history is recorded for dropped-but-visible group messages.
- **Prior context:** The access check and history recording were likely written at different times. The mention-gating path was added later with the correct pattern.
- **Why this regressed now:** This is not a regression — it has always been this way. The behavior becomes noticeable when users rely on `groupPolicy: "allowlist"` for access control while expecting the bot to maintain full group context.
- **If unknown, what was ruled out:** N/A

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- **Target test or file:** `monitor.channel-kind.test.ts` or `monitor.authz.test.ts`
- **Scenario the test should lock in:** When a non-allowlisted sender posts in a group with `groupPolicy: "allowlist"`, the message should be recorded to `channelHistories` but no response should be generated.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** A unit test on the monitor's message handling path can directly verify the history map is populated.
- **Existing test that already covers this:** None found.
- **If no new test is added, why not:** The existing test infrastructure for the monitor is complex. Adding a proper test requires familiarity with the test helpers and mocking patterns used in the project. Happy to add one with maintainer guidance.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Bots using `groupPolicy: "allowlist"` can now see messages from all group participants in their conversation context.
- Non-allowlisted users still cannot trigger bot responses (no change).
- When an allowlisted user @mentions the bot, the bot now has full group conversation context for better responses.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[non-allowlisted sender posts] -> [access check: NOT_ALLOWLISTED] -> [return] (no history recorded)
[allowlisted user asks "summarize"] -> [bot has no context] -> [cannot summarize]

After:
[non-allowlisted sender posts] -> [access check: set flag] -> [recordPendingHistory()] -> [return] (no response)
[allowlisted user asks "summarize"] -> [bot has full context] -> [accurate summary]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`
- Data access scope changed? `No` — messages were already received via WebSocket; this only affects whether they are stored in the in-memory pending history buffer.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 15.4 (Apple Silicon)
- Runtime/container: Node.js 25.8.1
- Model/provider: openai/gpt-5.4
- Integration/channel: Mattermost
- Relevant config (redacted):
  ```json
  {
    "channels": {
      "mattermost": {
        "chatmode": "oncall",
        "groupPolicy": "allowlist",
        "groupAllowFrom": ["<user-id>"],
        "historyLimit": 50
      }
    }
  }
  ```

### Steps

1. Configure Mattermost with `groupPolicy: "allowlist"` and one user in `groupAllowFrom`.
2. Have a non-allowlisted user send messages in the group.
3. Have the allowlisted user @mention the bot asking to summarize or reference those messages.

### Expected

Bot responds with context from all group messages, including non-allowlisted users.

### Actual

Before fix: Bot has no context of non-allowlisted user messages.
After fix: Bot correctly includes non-allowlisted messages in its context.

## Evidence

- [x] Trace/log snippets

Before: `mattermost: drop group sender=<id> (not in groupAllowFrom)` — no history recorded.
After: `mattermost: group sender=<id> not in groupAllowFrom (history-only)` followed by `mattermost: recorded history for blocked sender=<id>, not responding`.

## Human Verification (required)

- **Verified scenarios:** Tested with two Mattermost bot accounts, one allowlisted user, and multiple non-allowlisted users in a shared group channel. Confirmed bot can see and summarize non-allowlisted messages after patch.
- **Edge cases checked:** Verified non-allowlisted users still cannot trigger responses via @mention. Verified DM policy is unaffected. Verified other group policy modes (disabled, open) are unaffected.
- **What you did not verify:** Other channel plugins (Telegram, Signal, etc.) — this change only touches the Mattermost monitor.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk:** Increased memory usage from storing more history entries for high-traffic channels.
  - **Mitigation:** Bounded by the existing `historyLimit` setting (default 50). No unbounded growth.
- **Risk:** Non-allowlisted message content stored in memory could be seen by the bot in its responses.
  - **Mitigation:** This is the intended behavior — the bot already receives these messages via WebSocket. The change only affects whether they are available as context for future responses.

target.title: feat(irc): support markdown messages via draft/multiline
target.body:
## Summary

Adds support for sending markdown-formatted messages over IRC using the `draft/multiline` CAP extension. This preserves newlines in bot responses, allowing IRC clients to properly render markdown content.

## Motivation

OpenClaw bots typically generate markdown-formatted responses (lists, code blocks, paragraphs). Without multiline support, these get flattened into single lines, making them unreadable on IRC.

The `draft/multiline` spec (https://ircv3.net/specs/extensions/multiline) allows sending multiple lines as a single BATCH, which modern IRC clients can display with proper formatting.

## Changes

- **CAP negotiation**: Requests `draft/multiline` capability on connect, waits for ACK before sending
- **Outgoing BATCH**: Messages with newlines are sent as `BATCH +id draft/multiline #channel` with tagged PRIVMSGs
- **Incoming BATCH**: Multi-line messages received via BATCH are combined into single payload
- **Control chars**: Newlines (`0x0a`) preserved (previously stripped as IRC control chars)
- **Configurable limits**: `textChunkLimit` defaults to 16384 (per spec recommendation)

## Compatibility

- **Servers without draft/multiline**: Falls back to flattening newlines (existing behavior)
- **Clients without draft/multiline**: Will see lines individually (no worse than before)
- **Backwards compatible**: No config changes required

## Testing

Tested on Ergo IRC server with `draft/multiline` support. Bot responses with markdown (lists, code blocks) render correctly in supporting clients.

- provider/model, for example `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`

target.title: fix(ui): sync message delete to session transcript backend
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** Clicking the delete button on a message group in the Control UI only hid the message visually (localStorage) but left the backend .jsonl transcript untouched. The AI could still see the "deleted" content on the next turn.
- **Why it matters:** Users believe a message has been permanently removed, but the AI continues to respond based on that content -- a data inconsistency that creates both a confusing UX and a potential privacy risk.
- **What changed:** Added `sessions.truncate` RPC method, wired it through the protocol layer, gateway handler, and UI so that deleting a message actually truncates the backend transcript from that seq onward.
- **What did NOT change:** Existing `sessions.compact`, `sessions.reset`, or any other session mutation paths are untouched.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Memory / storage
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX

## Linked Issue/PR

- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History

- **Root cause:** The `onDelete` handler in the chat view only added the message group key to a localStorage-backed `DeletedMessages` set -- it never called any backend RPC to modify the .jsonl transcript.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** No integration test verified that deleting a message in the UI actually affected the transcript file.
- **Prior context:** The `sessions.compact` and `sessions.reset` RPC methods already existed with full protocol/handler/UI wiring; `truncate` was simply never added.
- **Why this regressed now:** The feature was never implemented; localStorage-only deletion was the original (incomplete) approach.

## Changes

### Backend (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts`)

Three-phase truncate with full safety:

1. **Phase 1** -- Read-only scan under `acquireSessionWriteLock` to locate the cut point. ENOENT-guarded. Does NOT abort active runs yet.
2. **Phase 2** -- Only if a valid cut exists: `cleanupSessionBeforeMutation` aborts active runs with `reason: "session-delete"`. If cleanup fails, the handler returns an error and the transcript is left untouched.
3. **Phase 3c** -- Re-acquire write lock, re-scan for seq (guards against concurrent `sessions.compact`), write-then-rename: writes truncated content to `.tmp.*`, renames original to `.bak.*`, renames temp to original. Preserves original file mode (`statSync(filePath).mode & 0o777`).

Additional safety:
- `rejectWebchatSessionMutation` gate blocks webchat clients (matching `sessions.patch`/`sessions.delete`)
- `reason: "truncate"` in `emitSessionsChanged` (not "compact")
- Token counts cleared on the session store entry after truncation

### Protocol layer

- `SessionsTruncateParamsSchema` with `key` (NonEmptyString) and `seq` (Integer, minimum: 1)
- AJV validator (`validateSessionsTruncateParams`) and type export
- Registered in `ProtocolSchemas`, `server-methods-list.ts`, and `method-scopes.ts` (operator.write)

### UI (`ui/src/ui/app-render.ts` + `ui/src/ui/views/chat.ts`)

- `onTruncateHistory(seq, onFail)` returns `boolean`: `false` when disconnected (caller skips optimistic hide), `true` when RPC dispatched
- `onFail` callback: called on RPC error OR `truncated: false`; caller's `deleted.restore(item.key)` reverses the optimistic hide
- Session-scoped: captures `state.sessionKey` at dispatch time; ignores `.then`/`.catch` if user navigated away
- Run-ID aware: captures `state.chatRunId` at dispatch; if a new run started during RPC flight, still reloads but does not clear the new run's state
- Only clears `chatMessages`/`chatStream`/`chatRunId` when `result.truncated === true`
- `.catch` does NOT clear chat history (only sets `lastError`)
- Search mode: delete disabled entirely when search is active (merged groups could silently drop non-adjacent history)
- When `__openclaw.seq` metadata is absent (e.g. live-streaming messages before history reload), `onDelete` is a no-op -- the user can retry after the chat reloads

### Swift models

- `SessionsTruncateParams` added to both `apps/macos` and `apps/shared` GatewayModels.swift

## Review Issues Addressed

All P1 and P2 issues from Greptile, Copilot, and Codex reviews have been addressed:

| # | Severity | Issue | Resolution |
|---|----------|-------|------------|
| 1 | P1 | Transcript loss if writeFileSync fails after rename | Write-then-rename: .tmp.* then .bak.* then rename |

target.title: feat(ios): add OpenClawMascot iconography system with size scale
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The iOS app has no formal mascot/iconography system. The OpenClaw mascot (claw creature) exists only as a small 180px `OpenClawIcon` asset used by a single `OpenClawProMark` component with hardcoded sizes. The style guide defines a full mascot size scale (96pt hero to 20pt inline), status badge composites, and a ghost variant for watermarks — none of which exist in code.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements section 03 (Iconography) of the iOS style guide. It adds:

- **High-resolution mascot asset** (512px source → proper 1x/2x/3x asset catalog) as `OpenClawMascot.imageset`
- **`OpenClawMascotScale` enum** with 6 predefined tiers: `.hero` (96pt), `.emptyState` (64pt), `.sheet` (44pt), `.section` (32pt), `.nav` (24pt), `.inline` (20pt)
- **`OpenClawMascot` view** that accepts either a scale tier or custom size, with automatic shadow
- **`OpenClawMascotBadge`** — mascot on a dark rounded surface with a semantic status badge overlay (connected ✓, pending ⧗, error ✗, info ↗, agent ✦, skill ◈, offline —, attention !)
- **`OpenClawMascotGhost`** — reduced-opacity mascot for empty states and watermarks
- **Migration** of 3 existing `OpenClawProMark` call sites to the new scale-based API

## User Impact

- Mascot rendering is higher quality (512px source vs 180px)
- Mascot sizes follow the style guide's predefined scale
- No visual behavior change at existing call sites (sizes map approximately: 28pt → `.nav` 24pt, 30pt → `.section` 32pt, 64pt → `.emptyState` 64pt)
- `OpenClawProMark` remains as a legacy wrapper for any external callers

## Evidence

### Build verification

```bash
# Clean build
rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/OpenClaw-*
pnpm ios:gen
cd apps/ios && xcodebuild -project OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClaw \
  -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro" build
# BUILD SUCCEEDED
```

### Asset verification

```
OpenClawMascot.imageset/
├── Contents.json          (1x/2x/3x with original rendering intent)
├── openclaw-mascot@1x.png (171×171)
├── openclaw-mascot@2x.png (341×341)
└── openclaw-mascot@3x.png (512×512)
```

Source: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/homarr-labs/dashboard-icons/png/openclaw-dark.png`

### Components added

| Component | Purpose | File |
|---|---|---|
| `OpenClawMascotScale` | Size scale enum (hero/emptyState/sheet/section/nav/inline) | `OpenClawMascot.swift` |
| `OpenClawMascot` | Core mascot view with scale + shadow | `OpenClawMascot.swift` |
| `OpenClawMascotBadge` | Mascot + semantic status badge overlay | `OpenClawMascot.swift` |
| `OpenClawMascotBadgeTone` | 8 status tones (connected/pending/error/info/agent/skill/offline/attention) | `OpenClawMascot.swift` |

target.title: fix(feishu): enforce configured webhookPath
target.body:
## Summary

Before this fix, the Feishu webhook HTTP handler accepted requests on ANY path hitting the configured port, as long as the signature was valid. This meant any attacker who could reach the webhook port and forge a valid signature could trigger event dispatch — an information leak and potential abuse vector.

Now the handler enforces `webhookPath` validation BEFORE signature verification, returning 404 for mismatched paths and 400 for malformed request targets.

## Changes

- Import `normalizeWebhookPath` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/webhook-path`
- Add `getWebhookRequestPath()` helper: validates origin-form request targets (`/path?query`), rejects absolute-form and network-path references (`//evil/path`)
- Normalize configured `webhookPath` before logging and matching (trims whitespace, ensures leading `/`, strips trailing `/`)
- Add path check in request handler: 400 for malformed targets, 404 for non-matching paths, both BEFORE signature verification
- Add comprehensive test suite (`monitor.transport.test.ts`) with 5 test cases

## Test Plan

- [x] Rejects requests on non-configured paths (404) before signature verification
- [x] Continues to accept requests on the configured path (200)
- [x] Does not treat `//host/path` request targets as matching (404)
- [x] Normalizes configured webhook paths before matching (strips whitespace/trailing slash)
- [x] Returns 400 instead of throwing on malformed absolute-form request targets
- [x] CI: check-test-types pass, dependency-guard-detect pass
- [x] CI: check-lint pass (verified locally)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: The Feishu webhook HTTP server accepted POST requests on ANY URL path, as long as the signature was valid. An attacker who could forge a valid Feishu signature could POST to `http://host:port/anything` and trigger event dispatch. Network-path references like `//evil.example.com/feishu/events` were treated as valid paths. There was no way to isolate the webhook to only the configured path.

**Real environment tested**: OpenClaw production instance (v2026.6.1, Node.js v22, Linux) with Feishu webhook configured on `127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Start Feishu webhook server with configured path /feishu/events
# 2. Send requests to verify path enforcement

# Wrong path — rejected with 404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/wrong-path \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Correct path — accepted (may fail at signature, not path)
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Network-path reference — rejected with 404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3000//evil/feishu/events" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Malformed absolute-form target — rejected with 400
$ echo -ne "POST http://[::1 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:3000\r\nConnection: close\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n" | nc 127.0.0.1 3000 | head -1
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/wrong-path -d '{}'
Not Found
HTTP 404

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events -d '{}'
Invalid signature
HTTP 401   # Path accepted (200), only fails at signature stage — correct behavior

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3000//evil/feishu/events" -d '{}'
Not Found
HTTP 404   # Network-path reference correctly rejected

$ echo -ne "POST http://[::1 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:3000\r\nConnection: close\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n" | nc 127.0.0.1 3000
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- Requests to wrong paths are rejected with 404 BEFORE signature verification — attacker cannot probe for valid paths via signature responses
- Network-path references (`//evil/path`) are correctly rejected
- Malformed absolute-form request targets return 400 instead of throwing
- Whitespace and trailing slashes in configured webhookPath are normalized: `" /feishu/events/ "` matches `/feishu/events`
- Query parameters on the configured path still work: `/feishu/events?source=test` is accepted
- All 5 unit test cases in `monitor.transport.test.ts` pass

**Not tested**: None for the behavior changed by this PR. Broader unrelated gateway/typecheck failures on current main are outside this PR scope.
